label: Dungeon level 1: room and corridor terrain, doors, stairs and room features
style: Hand-painted, realistic dark-fantasy game art in the manner of a gritty tactical RPG: muted earthy palette, believable weathered stone, oak and iron, painterly but precise. Shapes must stay readable when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.

rules.texture: A square game texture, orthographic: no perspective, no vanishing point, no horizon. Strong value contrast for a small, high-resolution game tile: light falls evenly from straight above, with no gradient, vignette or darker corners across the image, but deep ambient occlusion: every joint, gap and crack sinks into dark, almost black shadow, and the raised faces are lit, so each stone, plank or clod reads with a crisp dark outline. No text, no border, no frame.
rules.overlay: A game decal seen from directly above, looking straight down, orthographic. It lies flat on a floor that is not shown: everything that is not part of the object is fully transparent. Flat, even light, no cast shadow beyond the object. No text, no border.
rules.billboard: A single free-standing object for a game sprite, seen from the front and a little above (three-quarter view), centred, standing upright with its base on the bottom edge of the image and filling most of the width. Soft light from the upper left. Fully transparent background: no floor, no ground plane, no cast shadow, no text.

items.name: floor
items.prompt: Dungeon room floor seen from directly above: exactly four large square flagstones in a 2 by 2 grid filling the image, weathered grey-brown limestone with worn, slightly rounded edges, faint cracks, chips and scuffs. The joints between them are deep, narrow and dark, almost black. The joints run straight through the centre, one horizontal and one vertical, and along all four edges of the image, half a joint wide at each edge, so identical copies laid side by side make one continuous floor.

items.name: corridor
items.prompt: Dungeon corridor floor seen from directly above: rough, uneven packed earth and trampled grey-brown gravel with half-buried broken stones and pebbles and a few flat rocks, each stone sitting in its own dark shadowed hollow. Darker and rougher than a room floor. Detail spread evenly over the whole image with nothing large or distinctive, so it can repeat seamlessly.

items.name: stone
items.prompt: Solid undug bedrock seen from directly above: rough, fractured very dark grey-brown rock with natural cracks and a few faint mineral veins. Detail spread evenly, nothing large or distinctive, uniform brightness, so it can repeat seamlessly.

items.name: wall
items.prompt: A dungeon wall seen straight on: roughly dressed grey-brown stone blocks laid in exactly three horizontal courses, each course one third of the image high, with dark recessed mortar joints along the top and bottom edges of the image. In every course a vertical joint falls exactly on the left edge and on the right edge of the image, with one or two more joints inside the course, staggered between courses. Each block bulges slightly, lit on its face and falling into shadow at its edges; the joints are deep and nearly black. Chipped block edges, damp staining, a few small patches of moss.

items.name: door

items.prompt: A heavy dungeon door seen straight on, filling the entire square edge to edge with no wall or frame around it: vertical dark oak planks, two black iron strap hinges running across, rows of iron studs, an iron ring pull at the middle of the right side, worn, scratched and darkened by age.

items.name: open_door
items.refNote: Image 1 is the face of the door, for material and colour only.
items.prompt: This same door standing wide open, seen from directly above, looking straight down onto its top edge. Nothing else is painted: the rest of the image is fully transparent.

items.name: stairs_down

Image 2 is the matching up staircase already painted for this dungeon: use exactly its honey-orange oak, red-brown shadows, iron nails and painting style.
items.prompt: A square stairwell opening seen from directly above, looking straight down into it, filling most of the image: a frame of dark, heavy timber beams around the edge, and inside it a flight of honey-orange oak steps descending away into deep darkness, each tread lit warm on top with a dark shadowed riser below, the lowest steps fading into black. Nothing outside the timber frame is painted: everything outside it is fully transparent.

items.name: stairs_up
items.refNote: Image 1 is the pixel-art up staircase from the tileset this art replaces. Keep its idea, silhouette and colours, but paint it as realistic, hand-painted game art; ignore its square background and the blocky pixels.
items.prompt: A free-standing flight of sturdy wooden steps, seen from the front and slightly from the side: one solid stepped block rising from the lower left to the upper right in five steps, its highest step simply ending at the top, with nothing above or beyond it: no door, no archway, no opening, no hatch and no light source. Warm honey-orange oak treads lit from above, darker red-brown risers and sides in shadow, iron nails and worn edges. It must stand out clearly against a grey stone floor.
